AUSENTE behavior of depth helpers and bypass dispatch enable and retire and idle renotify beyond call ordering shown.
AUSENTE full layouts of scheduler and per processor and runqueue and task extension records beyond fields mentioned.
AUSENTE reason strings for exit kinds and default watchdog timeouts and backtrace and message capacities.

findings.text: Toggling bypass on a scheduler propagates a depth count to every descendant so that a node bypasses when itself or any ancestor requests it, refreshes per processor bypass markers for all possible processors, requeues runnable members of the affected subtree to honor the new mode, and enables or retires the bypass dispatch structures around the transition.

Bypass changes serialize with an interrupt saved bypass lock held for the whole operation, take the scheduler hierarchy lock to adjust descendant depths and per processor markers, and then for each possible processor hold the runqueue lock while updating markers and cycling tasks, dropping the auxiliary runqueue reference before releasing.

Entering bypass preserves forward progress by explicitly ending the slice of a currently running member while leaving queued members to a dequeue and enqueue cycle without changing task properties, skipping tasks whose owning scheduler lies outside the target subtree and requesting rescheduling on online or local processors.

Leaving bypass retires normal dispatch structures only after all processors were visited which prevents tasks remaining on bypass queues, and the walk covers every possible processor rather than relying on a lock that cannot be trusted while the scheduler is suspect.

Replay of effective capacity state after leaving bypass expects the runqueue lock held, ignores the root level which never uses that state, returns early when reported and desired values already match, and otherwise takes the per shard lock for the processor capacity domain before queuing a synchronization.

Exit information bundles an exit processor marker initialized to absent, a fixed length backtrace area, a fixed length message area, and a variable length dump area, with any partial allocation failure releasing the whole bundle and reporting absence.

Release of per processor kick synchronization first flushes pending processor kick work, then atomically replaces the stored pointer with absent and defers reclamation through a read copy update callback when an object was present.

Watchdog maintenance derives its interval as half of the smallest configured scheduler timeout bounded below by a single tick, records the current time and interval with single store semantics under read protection, and arms or cancels the shared delayed work depending on whether any scheduler remains.

Linking registers a scheduler in the global list and refreshes the watchdog, while a scheduler with a parent additionally inserts into a global hash and attaches to the parent child list. Unlinking reverses those steps under the hierarchy lock and again refreshes the watchdog.

Linking refuses when the parent currently bypasses or is aborting, backing out hash and sibling linkage on the abort path, and marks successful parent attachment with a linked flag that later determines whether disable must rehome cgroups and tasks.

Disabling dump state sets a disabled marker under an interrupt saved dump lock, while disable logging distinguishes a top scheduler from a nested one and reports errors with reason plus message and backtrace versus informational notice for orderly exits.

Root disable moves from bypass plus descendant drain through a disabling enable state into a mutex protected teardown that switches every task off the extension class, clears global enable markers and idle support, synchronizes, invokes scheduler exit, marks the object dead, unlinks, clears the root pointer with capacity table retirement, removes system objects, frees kick state, and finally leaves bypass.

Nested disable bypasses only itself, drains descendants, then under enable and fork and cgroup protection returns its cgroup subtree to the parent and rehomes each member task onto the parent, before dump disable, expedited synchronization, bypass dispatch retirement, unlink, waiter wakeup, detach notification, exit invocation and system object removal.

Rehoming preserves queue position while exiting the old scheduler and initializing on the new one through begin and init and ready stages with an enable step when the task remains in the extension class. Punting instead only exits and retargets the owner and requires the destination already bypassing.

Failure to initialize a moving task on the parent records a parent error, bypasses the parent to permit progress, and punts every remaining member of the dying subtree into the parent without per task initialization.

Return of a nested cgroup subtree uses a bottom up pass to invoke exit where initialized and transfer ownership to the parent with a temporary marker, followed by a top down pass that clears the marker and attempts parent initialization, with a sticky parent failure flag causing later groups to stay uninitialized for onward movement.
Assignment of a scheduler to a cgroup subtree updates the stored scheduler pointer for every live descendant cgroup under read copy update semantics.

Asynchronous disable starts with a preemption guarded claim that queues interrupt work, while the worker claims the stored exit kind exactly once from pending to done, records kind and textual reason, and dispatches to nested or root teardown based on parent presence. Exit propagation walks descendants and requests disable for each.
Descendant drain waits until the child list of the target becomes empty, relying on recursive disable to remove each proper descendant when it reaches unlinking.
Built in idle shutdown clears the two global idle enable markers for normal and per node operation.
Builds without nested scheduler support replace cgroup assignment and descendant drain and nested disable and capacity replay and subtree return with empty operations that perform no state change.
